The repo is essentially empty — a playground project with OMGithub tooling. The user wants a platformer game. I need to build a browser game from scratch. There's a start.sh that runs the default start script from RUNTIME_DIR. probably a static server serving the repo at port 3002.

Let me check the runtime dir and how to preview/capture. Also check playwright-cli availability.

Plan: Build a single-page HTML5 canvas platformer game, vanilla JS, no dependencies (safer than bundlers). Features requested:
- fight monsters
- collect mushrooms
- unlock armor
- defeat bosses

I should make it polished and fun: multiple levels, sprites drawn with canvas shapes, physics, combat (melee sword), mushrooms as currency/collectibles, armor upgrades purchasable/equippable, boss fights at end of levels.

Let me design:

Game: "Sporefall" or "Mycelia" — a mushroom knight platformer. Theme: enchanted forest, glowing mushrooms. Player is a little knight with a cape. Collect mushrooms (currency), unlock armor tiers (Leather, Iron, Crystal) giving health/defense, fight slimes, bats, spitters, and bosses (e.g., giant toad / mushroom king / root golem).

Tech: single index.html + style.css + js modules? For simplicity, use a modular set of JS files loaded as ES modules, served statically. No build step. Use canvas 2D with camera, particle effects, screen shake, parallax background, procedural audio via WebAudio.

Scope: To be achievable and high quality within time, build:
- Engine: fixed timestep loop, input (keyboard + touch), AABB physics tile collision.
- Level data as ASCII grids, 3 levels + boss arena maybe 3 levels each with a boss at end. Or 4 levels: Forest (tutorial, boss: Slime King), Caverns (boss: Bat Queen), Ruins (boss: Root Golem), maybe final.
- Mushrooms: collectibles that give coins; spend at armor forge checkpoints? Simpler: mushrooms collected unlock armor automatically at thresholds, with a forge UI accessible via pause? User said "collect mushrooms, unlock armor" — make mushrooms currency to buy 3 armor tiers at a forge station, or automatic unlock. I'll do: mushrooms spendable at Forge (a station in levels) with UI overlay; also auto-equip.

Better UX: Armor unlocks automatically when you have enough mushrooms (thresholds 10, 25, 45), with a toast and stat boost. But buying is more interactive. Let's implement a Forge shrine: stand near it, press E/Tap, shop opens with armor pieces to buy (helmet, chestplate) — maybe keep it simple: 3 armor sets with cost, each gives +max HP and damage reduction and changes appearance. Mushrooms persist across levels. This is engaging.

Controls: A/D or arrows move, Space/W jump, J/click attack, K/Shift dash, E interact. Touch: on-screen buttons.

Enemies:
- Slime: patrols, damages on contact, can be stomped (Mario-style) or sworded.
- Bat: sine flight, chases when near.
- Spitter plant: stationary, fires projectiles.
- Beetle: walks, armored, needs 2 hits.
- Bosses: patterns with phases, health bar.

Combat: sword swing with arc, hitbox, knockback, particles, damage numbers. Player has 5 HP base, invincibility frames, respawn at checkpoint with mushrooms retained but maybe lose some? Keep forgiving: no loss, respawn at last checkpoint. Death resets level enemies? Simple respawn at checkpoint with full health.

HUD: hearts, mushroom count, armor name, level name, boss health bar.

Screens: Title → level intro → play → level complete → final victory. Pause menu. Settings: mute, controls.

Juice: particles, camera follow with smoothing, screen shake, hit flash, parallax, ambient spores, fireflies, vignette, CRT? Use gradients, silhouettes.

Visuals: Draw with canvas primitives but carefully crafted: gradient sky, layered parallax hills/trees, tile textures with noise-ish detail, character with animated limbs (procedural). Aim for charming pixel-ish/vector look.

I need to ensure it runs. Test with playwright screenshot. Let me check the environment: node version, playwright-cli, port.

    inputs:
      issue_number:

        required: true

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}

jobs:

    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write

      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write

Static html. Good. I'll build plain HTML/CSS/JS with no build. Serve via start.sh (port 3000? default PORT=3000, while Agents.md says 3002; I'll just run node default-start with PORT=3002 manually).

Let me now plan the game carefully and write it.

Architecture files:
- index.html: canvas, UI overlays (title, HUD, shop, pause, death, victory), touch controls.
- styles.css: full-screen layout, fonts (system + Google? offline safe — use local system fonts, maybe embed a font? Use CSS font stack with "Georgia"/serif for fantasy and system sans). Could use Google Fonts but risky offline. Use local.
- src/main.js: bootstrap, loop, state machine.
- src/input.js
- src/audio.js (WebAudio procedural SFX/music)
- src/level.js (level definitions ASCII, tilemap)
- src/entities.js (player, enemies, boss, projectiles, pickups)
- src/render.js (background, tiles, UI draw)
- src/particles.js
- maybe src/game.js coordinating.

Given tool constraints, I can write moderate-sized files. Need to be careful about bugs. Maybe simpler to have fewer files to avoid circular imports: 
- main.js (loop/state)
- input.js
- audio.js
- levels.js
- game.js (world/entities/physics/combat)
- render.js (drawing)
- ui.js? HUD handled in render + DOM overlays in index.html.

Let me design gameplay specifics.

World units: tiles 48px? Canvas internal resolution scaled. Use virtual resolution 960x540 with letterbox scaling? Better responsive: render at CSS size * DPR, camera based on height ~ 600 units. Simpler: fixed world camera zoom such that view height = 540 units; canvas scaled. Use design resolution 960x540 letterboxed to fit window (cover? contain). For mobile portrait, contain means tiny. Hmm mobile support required. Could adapt: use camera view height based on aspect: view height 540 minimum, width = 540*aspect. For portrait phone (390x844 -> aspect 0.46), width would be 250 — too narrow for platformer. Instead support landscape suggestion overlay on portrait? Agents.md says support phones/tablets responsive with usable touch. Do a rotate prompt for portrait small screens, but still functional with letterbox. Many mobile games ask landscape. I'll implement: canvas fills screen; camera view height 560, width derived; if portrait, show "Rotate for best experience" hint and scale HUD. Gameplay still playable with view width ~300, but levels designed for wider. Better: set camera view width = clamp(720, aspect*560), so min width 720 and extra vertical space... For portrait that means view height = 720/aspect = 1560 huge zoom out. Not good.

Alternative: fixed virtual canvas 960x540 and CSS letterbox "contain"; on portrait, game occupies width 390 -> height 219 in middle, small but playable with touch buttons below/overlay. Hmm not great.

Let's do adaptive camera: zoom = max(1, 540/viewHeightCSS)? Let's think in terms of world units shown. Use scale = canvasHeight / 560 for landscape; for portrait, design for canvasWidth/720 so width >= 720? On 390x844 portrait, scale = 390/720 = 0.54, viewHeight world = 844/0.54 = 1560 world units — huge, showing too much vertically but tiles are 48 so ~32 tiles tall. Levels aren't that tall. Not harmful but weird.

Better approach: encourage landscape via overlay for portrait: "Rotate device" screen with button "Play anyway". Landscape phone 844x390: view height 390/scale. Keep world view height ~ 500 → scale 0.78, view width 1082. That's fine. On desktop 1440x900: view height 560, width 896. Good.

So: world view height = 560 (units), scale = canvasCSSHeight/560, camera view width = canvasCSSWidth/scale = 560*aspect. For portrait aspect 0.46 → width 258. Levels would feel cramped. Add rotate hint overlay in portrait that auto-hides on rotate, with a dismiss. Playable if dismissed.

Simplify: choose viewWidth = 960 fixed for landscape-ish; scale = canvasWidth/960, viewHeight = canvasHeight/scale. On desktop 16:9: 540. On 4:3: 720. On portrait: 2077 tall. That's too tall. So instead camera centers on player and clamps to level bounds; extra vertical space just shows sky/underground. Could be acceptable? A portrait view 960 wide and 2077 tall would zoom way out and see whole level vertically. Bad.

Let's just do: internal design resolution 960x540 scaled with CSS "contain" letterbox. Portrait gets letterboxed to a small strip. Add rotate prompt. Mobile landscape is the main mobile case. That's clean, consistent art direction, and simplest. But 390x844 portrait playable region 390x219 — with touch controls overlaid maybe too small. I'll add portrait overlay suggesting rotation that blocks play; if user dismisses, still letterboxed. Hmm, blocking might annoy mobile screenshot tests (capture only screenshots at 390x844 → would show rotate prompt, bad for showcase). The default capture takes mobile screenshot. Better mobile screenshot should look good. So make portrait responsive, not just prompt.

Alternative: responsive camera with different target sizes while keeping art: viewHeight = clamp(500, 560, ...). Use `zoom = min(canvasW/960, canvasH/540)` (contain) but for portrait, zoom based on width 960 gives tiny height ... same.

Hmm, what do good mobile platformers do in portrait? They design levels vertically or use wide-ish view. We can simply use "cover" scaling for portrait: camera view width fixed at 640 world units for mobile, height = 640/aspect = 1385. Showing high sky and deep ground; with level geometry based around y, we can clamp camera and it shows big empty regions. If backgrounds and vignette handle it, maybe okay but player tiny relative? Player is 40 units in 640 wide view = 6% of width; on 390px screen, 24px tall sprite. Too small.

Better for portrait: view width 420 world units, height 420/0.462=909 world units. Then scale 390/420=0.93, player 40 units→37px. Vertical view huge: 19 tiles. Could design levels with tall verticality; camera follows. But level height maybe 20 tiles = 960. Fits. Actually that's workable! messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a browser platformer game where the player fights monsters, collects mushrooms, unlocks armor, and defeats bosses.

## Requirements
- User request only: "Platformer game where you fight monsters, collect mushrooms, unlock armor, and defeat bosses."
- Must run as a static site from repo root; existing `start.sh` expects `index.html`.
- Mobile-responsive (portrait/landscape phones, tablets) with usable touch controls.
- Visual quality should be strong; title and gameplay screenshots must be presentable at desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844.

## Decisions
- Built vanilla HTML/CSS/JS ES modules with no build step or dependencies.
- Game concept: **Sporefall**, a mushroom-knight platformer with 3 chapters and 3 bosses.
- Mechanics: sword combat, stompable enemies, mushroom currency, 3 purchasable armor tiers at forge stations, checkpoints, dash, double jump at tier 3, boss arenas, level exits, victory screen.
- Armor prices: 10 / 25 / 45 spores; armor grants +1/+2/+3 hearts and tier 3 grants +1 sword damage and a midair jump.
- Visuals are procedurally drawn Canvas 2D with parallax forest/cavern/summit themes, particles, glows, screen shake, hitstop, procedural WebAudio music/SFX.
- Canvas view scaling: portrait uses `scale = width/500`; landscape/desktop uses `min(width/1000, height/560)` clamped 0.58–2.2.
- Primary title button text is exactly "Play" so the capture harness auto-start heuristic clicks it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full game code:
  - `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`
  - `src/constants.js`, `src/physics.js`, `src/levels.js`, `src/effects.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/audio.js`
  - `src/entities.js` (Player, Enemy, Boss, Projectile, Pickup)
  - `src/game.js` (state machine, levels, shop, checkpoints, death/respawn, boss flow, save/continue)
  - `src/render.js` (themes, parallax, tiles, props, player/enemies/bosses, particles, UI overlays via DOM)
- Implemented 3 levels:
  - Mossgrove (`slimeKing`, 50 HP)
  - Hollow Caverns (`batQueen`, 62 HP)
  - Sporefall Summit (`mushroomMonarch`, 88 HP)
- Implemented title/shop/pause/clear/victory overlays, HUD, boss bar, toasts, level cards, touch controls.
- Verified with headless Playwright:
  - No page errors or console errors.
  - Title → Play → gameplay works.
  - Forge opens with `e`, armor purchase works (10 spores → Barkbound Mail, max HP 3→4).
  - All 3 bosses spawn, take damage, die; door unlocks; clear overlay and level transitions work.
  - Death/respawn works.
  - Touch buttons move player on portrait/landscape/tablet.
- Screenshots captured: title, gameplay, shop, purchased armor, all bosses, mobile portrait/landscape/tablet.

### Active
- Visual/gameplay polish based on screenshot review.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix minor visual/UX issues:
   - Level card overlaps boss HUD/toast during fast transitions (only test artifacts; acceptable but can lower priority).
   - Toast currently overlaps shop panel; a `body.is-paused .toast { top: 82px; bottom: auto; }` rule was added but needs visual re-check.
   - Title knight now stands at world x `12.5*TILE` facing left; verify framing remains good.
   - Some cave/summit screens feel sparse; optional extra foreground decoration.
2. Validate level traversability/jump reachability (platforms were adjusted to ≤2 tiles above surfaces, but not run through a formal validator).
3. Test full natural gameplay path without teleports (jump gaps, spikes, boss fairness, checkpoint respawn).
4. Test final victory screen (`winGame`) and "Play again"/title flows.
5. Capture final screenshots with `capture.sh` / `playwright-cli` if needed; confirm mobile HUD/touch safe areas.
6. Update `README.md` with a short game description while preserving the `omgithub:readme` markers.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM/canvas layout, overlays, HUD, touch controls, title/shop/victory markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full visual design, responsive layout, overlays, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: central state machine, levels, shop, combat glue, save/continue, boss/death/level flow.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities.js`: player physics/combat, enemies, bosses, projectiles, pickups.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: all Canvas rendering, themes, parallax, characters, effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/levels.js`: level builder, level definitions, entity/tile placement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/constants.js`: TILE=48, physics constants, ARMOR definitions, helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/physics.js`: shared tile collision and spike hazard checks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio SFX and music.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: keyboard mapping, virtual/touch input, touch binding.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: particle bursts/dust/spores, ambient mote generation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: bootstrap, `window.game`, touch device class.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: still original OMGithub readme; needs game blurb.
- `/tmp/opencode/test.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/debug.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/boss.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/mobile.mjs`: throwaway Playwright test scripts.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/`: screenshots from verification runs.

## Important Context
- Local server is running in tmux session `spore`:
  `tmux new-session -d -s spore "cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround && PORT=3002 /usr/bin/time -p node $RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs > /tmp/opencode/spore-server.log 2>&1"`
  URL: `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Playwright available via:
  `createRequire(process.env.HOME + '/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/package.json')`.
- In Playwright, press `'e'`, `'j'`, `'Space'`, etc. — `press('KeyE')` did **not** trigger game interaction.
- Tests teleport via `page.evaluate(() => { game.player.x = ...; game.snapCamera(); ... })`; `window.game` is exposed.
- Known potential issue: `body.is-paused` class is set for paused/shop and blurs canvas; shop screenshot looked good.
- Boss arena camera bounds now include `{x0,x1,y0,y1}`; this fixed an earlier NaN camera bug.
- `Game` constructor no longer starts music before a user gesture; music starts on Play.
- Active save key: `sporefall.save.v1` (localStorage); saves on level load, checkpoint, armor purchase, boss defeat, victory.
- Server log: `/tmp/opencode/spore-server.log`.
- No git commit has been made for the game files; working tree changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a browser platformer game where the player fights monsters, collects mushrooms, unlocks armor, and defeats bosses.

## Requirements
- User request only: "Platformer game where you fight monsters, collect mushrooms, unlock armor, and defeat bosses."
- Must run as a static site from repo root; existing `start.sh` expects `index.html`.
- Mobile-responsive (portrait/landscape phones, tablets) with usable touch controls.
- Visual quality should be strong; title and gameplay screenshots must be presentable at desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844.

## Decisions
- Built vanilla HTML/CSS/JS ES modules with no build step or dependencies.
- Game concept: **Sporefall**, a mushroom-knight platformer with 3 chapters and 3 bosses.
- Mechanics: sword combat, stompable enemies, mushroom currency, 3 purchasable armor tiers at forge stations, checkpoints, dash, double jump at tier 3, boss arenas, level exits, victory screen.
- Armor prices: 10 / 25 / 45 spores; armor grants +1/+2/+3 hearts and tier 3 grants +1 sword damage and a midair jump.
- Visuals are procedurally drawn Canvas 2D with parallax forest/cavern/summit themes, particles, glows, screen shake, hitstop, procedural WebAudio music/SFX.
- Canvas scaling: portrait uses `scale = max(width/500, height/900)`; landscape/desktop uses `min(width/1000, height/560)` clamped 0.58–2.2.
- Primary title button text is exactly "Play" so the capture harness auto-start heuristic clicks it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game built: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/constants.js`, `src/physics.js`, `src/levels.js`, `src/effects.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/entities.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/render.js`.
- Three levels with bosses: Mossgrove (`slimeKing`, 50 HP), Hollow Caverns (`batQueen`, 56 HP), Sporefall Summit (`mushroomMonarch`, 88 HP).
- Title/shop/pause/clear/victory overlays, HUD, boss bar, toasts, level cards, touch controls implemented.
- Verified no page/console errors; title → Play → gameplay works; forge opens via `e`; armor purchase works; checkpoints, death/respawn, boss defeat, door unlock, level transitions, and victory work.
- Fixed boss camera framing by targeting midpoint between player and boss while a boss is active.
- Fixed shop toast overlap by replacing the global toast with inline `#shopNotice`.
- Improved ground rendering with cached procedural ground textures, moss/grass surface details, exposed-edge roots, themed platform variants, foreground flora, weather particles, abyss darkening, and boss danger vignette.
- Fixed portrait framing with taller scale so ground fills more of the screen.
- Added touch-specific control hints (replaces keyboard hints on touch devices).
- Fixed lingering level card when returning to title; level cards now hide on boss trigger and level load.
- Fixed critical Bat Queen bug where state stayed `idle` forever; she now enters `hover`, dives to ground, enters a punishable `recover` state, and is hittable with normal jump attacks.
- Rebalanced Bat Queen: lower hover height, 0.8s recover window, 56 HP.
- Verified all three bosses can be defeated with actual sword attacks; all door/clear/victory transitions work.
- Verified all levels are traversable with enemies disabled using a natural movement bot (no falls once ledge-jump logic added).
- Static level validator confirms all standable surfaces reachable, no embedded pickups, no gaps wider than 3 tiles.
- Mobile checks: 390×844 title/gameplay/shop fit; shop scrolls at 320×568 by design.

### Active
- Final visual/mobile polish and final verification screenshots.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add `touch-action: pan-y` to `.shop-panel` on mobile to ensure touch scrolling works at 320×568.
2. Re-run final desktop/mobile screenshot capture and inspect title, gameplay, shop (including purchase notice), all three boss arenas, victory, and touch controls.

4. Update `README.md` with a short Sporefall description while preserving the `omgithub:readme` markers.
5. Verify final `git status`; all game files remain uncommitted.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: all Canvas rendering, themes, tile/flora/weather effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities.js`: player, enemies, boss AI; recent Bat Queen fixes.
